solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Doctor climbed up and down

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a standard crossword doctor
past tense of rise, to go upwards

explanation.surface: A doctor going up and down, perhaps on stairs or a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' looks like a single phrase about movement, but 'down' alone is the definition, meaning low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means gloomy and sullen in mood, which is exactly what a morose person is.

clue.text: Come and go around ancient kingdom

indicators.note: to go around is to move about, so the letters before it are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words are used

explanation.surface: Visitors arriving and leaving around some old realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was the realm in northern Greece ruled by Philip II and his son Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Drums for Highland dances

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cylinders on which thread, film or cable is wound
second meaning: lively Scottish folk dances

explanation.surface: Drumming to accompany dancing in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drums' looks like percussion for the dancers, but it is the plural noun for winding spools.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable and fishing line are wound on spools, and Scottish country dancing includes quick dances of the same name.

clue.text: Has arrested a criminal in arid area

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: Police have caught a lawbreaker somewhere in a dry region.
explanation.definitionFit: The great North African waste of sand and rock is the best-known example of a dry, barren region.

clue.text: Old boy regularly loses instrument

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A former pupil keeps losing his musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a double-reed woodwind with a penetrating tone, the one that sounds the tuning note for an orchestra.

clue.text: Catch husband with parent: capital

parts.note: to bag is to catch or capture, as game
H is the abbreviation for husband
an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Landing a husband who comes with a parent attached, as a matrimonial catch.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Iraq, standing on the Tigris.

clue.text: Soil the planet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ground or dirt plants grow in
second meaning: the world we live on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' reads like a verb, as in to pollute the planet, but it is a noun meaning dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both garden dirt and our own world, the third planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Very keen psalmist loses his head

indicators.note: losing one's head means the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic hymn writer gets carried away and loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and enthusiastic, as in an avid reader.

clue.text: Attend a corps feast, then leave hurriedly

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a treat is a special meal or delight

explanation.surface: Turn up to a regimental banquet, then slip away quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a corps of the British Army; the military flavour of the surface matches the answer's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a drum signal ordering troops to withdraw, and now means to withdraw in haste.

clue.text: Writer of plays: mark as completed for audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the phrase is judged by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to check off an item is to tick it as done

explanation.surface: A dramatist ticks items off a list in front of a theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was the Russian dramatist of The Seagull, Uncle Vanya and The Cherry Orchard.

clue.text: Composer locked in hotel garage

indicators.note: locked in means shut inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A musician has been shut inside a hotel's car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Tired out after recording? Shame

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the one that follows it in the clue

parts.note: a record or CD is a disc

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician exhausted after a studio session feels ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired out' looks like a single phrase meaning exhausted, but 'out' is working alone on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring shame on someone is to damage their reputation and good name, which is what the word means as a verb or noun.

clue.text: A note sounded by Homer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first note of the sol-fa scale
second meaning: the exclamation of annoyance made by Homer Simpson

explanation.walkthrough: Homer suggests the Greek epic poet, but it is the cartoon father in The Simpsons, whose catchphrase is now in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sol-fa name for the keynote of a scale, and also the cry of frustration Homer Simpson utters.

clue.text: Unimportant person's criticism of thin wine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone of no significance
second meaning, read as two words: a wine taster complaining it lacks fullness

explanation.walkthrough: Wine tasters speak of a wine's body, its fullness; a thin wine has none, and the question mark flags that playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance is called a nonentity, and split in two the word is a taster's verdict that a wine lacks weight.

clue.text: Looks embarrassed, left in the undergrowth

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: shrubs forming low thick growth
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in the shrubbery looks awkward and ashamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed reddens in the face, so the verb is a fair match for showing embarrassment.

clue.text: Newly-wed adopts golf, a tricky game

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a woman on her wedding day or just married
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newlywed takes up golf and finds it a difficult sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game for two partnerships with bidding and trumps is famously demanding to play well.

clue.text: Almost sooner than expected, make millions out of title

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: arriving before the expected time
to do is to make or perform
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone cashes in a peerage for a fortune earlier than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the rank and territory of an earl, a hereditary title of the British nobility.

clue.text: Small coin once inadequate for Arab market

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the final letter of the following word is cut off

parts.note: a souk is a market in an Arab town

explanation.surface: A tiny old coin would not go far in a Middle Eastern bazaar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou was an old French coin of low value, still used in the phrase not a sou.

clue.text: Scrape mark, small, on end of sleeve

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the cuff is the band at the end of a sleeve

explanation.surface: A little mark rubbed on a shirt cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuff is a mark made by scraping or rubbing a surface, as on shoes or furniture.

clue.text: Elastic sort of brick?

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun, fair because an elastic is also used as a noun for a stretchy band, something that stretches
definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that extends, as an elastic does
second meaning: a brick laid with its long side along the face of a wall

explanation.walkthrough: In bricklaying, bricks laid lengthwise are one name and those laid end-on are headers; the question mark admits the stretchy first sense is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that lengthens can be called by the word, and bricklayers use it for a brick showing its long face.

clue.text: Wholly engrossed, knocked sharply to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means judged by sound, so the phrase is replaced by a word pronounced the same

parts.note: to rap is to strike smartly, as on a door

explanation.surface: Someone so absorbed they only notice a sharp knock at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt describes someone completely absorbed and enthralled, as in rapt attention.

clue.text: Swell in endless bliss

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter of the following word is removed

parts.note: heaven is a state of perfect happiness

explanation.surface: Swelling with joy in a state of perfect happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like the dated slang for excellent, but it is the verb for rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea is said to rise and fall in a long swell, so the verb fits a surging upward movement.

clue.text: Escort's two pronouns

parts.note: the first pronoun: the plural first-person object form
the second pronoun: the feminine object form

explanation.surface: A grammar note about the pronouns an escort uses.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone to their seat or guide them in is to escort them, as at a wedding or theatre.

clue.text: Sort of chart, plain black and white

parts.note: a pie chart shows proportions as slices of a circle
bald means plain and unadorned, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: A simple monochrome diagram, as printed without colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes a horse with irregular patches of black and white.

clue.text: Stuck, showing the wrong time

definitions.meaning: second meaning: describing a clock that runs ahead

explanation.surface: A clock that has jammed and shows the wrong hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A stuck clock suggests one that is slow or stopped, but the answer is a clock running ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fixed firmly in place, and of a clock or watch it means reading later than the true time.

clue.text: Master reorganised pupils' group

indicators.note: reorganised means arranged differently, so the letters of the word before it are reordered

parts.note: the letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster reshuffles the classes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools pupils are often streamed: divided into ability groups called streams.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools sort children by ability into sets, and each such band of pupils is called by this word.
